newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Former Venezuela beauty queen sets sights on power.
newsitem.headline: Former Venezuela beauty queen sets sights on power.

text.p: A former Miss Universe who is Venezuela's most popular politician has formed a movement aimed at taking her to victory in presidential elections next year, she said in an interview published on Friday.

"This is happening is a spontaneous way. Hundreds of thousands of signatures have been collected," Irene Saez said in a television interview on Thursday night. "I know that to reach (the palace) one needs an organisation and a well organised structure."

The interview was the clearest indication yet that the 34-year-old blonde, who won the Miss Universe title in 1981 and is currently mayor of the Caracas district Chacao, has set her sights on the country's top job.
"The only way for me to stop would be that the people say 'The hope is not Irene, it is somebody else,'" she said.

Opinion polls rate Saez as the leading potential candidate in Venezuela for the December 1998 presidential polls with levels of support far ahead of traditional politicians. But her critics have dubbed her a "Barbie doll" with a fuzzy political platform and say her popularity would evaporate if she left Chacao, known locally as "Irenelandia."
